title: Two requests, one row
question: Two requests changed the same row at the same moment. Which one won, and what did the other lose?
summary: What a transaction actually promises, and the read-then-write that loses an update inside one anyway. Every rep is a fix you would ship: a conditional update, an upsert, a retry. Ends with a booking system that sold the last place twice.

steps.note: The shapes that survive concurrency, once you know the transaction alone does not.
Two connections, one last place, and a count kept beside the rows it counts.
